 Judgment

This appeal is by the appellants-claimants seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 05.04.2016 passed in M.V.C. No. 114/2013 on the file of the MACT-XII, Ballari (for short 'the Tribunal').
2. Brief facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that:
The appellants have filed a claim petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of one Sreepathi in a road accident occurred on 13.08.2012.

It is averred that when the deceased was proceeding in his TVS Excel Moped motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-34-W-1224 on Ballari-Bangalore road, a tractor- trialer bearing reg. no. KA-34-B-555 and KA-34-C-555 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner collided with the motorcycle resulted in falling of the deceased on the road and sustaining grievous injuries.
Later he succumbed to those injuries in the hospital.

It is further averred that the deceased was hail and healthy prior to the accident, was aged 65 years, was an Ex-Serviceman from the Indian Army, getting pension of Rs.3,430/- per month and was also drawing Rs.5,000/- as NC: 2023:KHC-D:13208-DB pension from the State Bank of Mysore.
Due to his sudden death, the appellants have suffered mentally, physically and financially and hence sought for compensation.
Respondents no.2 to 4 have filed separate written statements before the Tribunal.

All of them have denied the averments made in the claim petition, denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased and averred that the respondent no.1 was not holding valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident.
Thus the respondent no.4 is not liable to pay compensation.
The Tribunal has framed issues and recorded evidence of the parties.
The claimant no.1 examined himself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.17.
The respondents have examined R.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.7.
The Tribunal on considering the evidence on record has awarded a sum of Rs.3,52,560/- as total compensation.

Being aggrieved by the same,

3. Sri T. Basavana Goud, learned counsel for the appellants- claimants submits that the Tribunal committed error in assessing income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month as the deceased was an Ex-Serviceman and drawing pension of NC: 2023:KHC-D:13208-DB Rs.3,430/- per month and was also getting pension from the State Bank of Mysore where he was working after retirement from the services of the Indian Army which is evident from EX.P10 and P11.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding lower compensation on other heads.
He seeks for enhancement of compensation by allowing the appeal.

4. Per contra, Sri Nagaraj C. Kolloori, learned counsel for the respondent No.4-insurer supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the Tribunal was justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month as the appellants have failed to produce any evidence before the Tribunal.

It is submitted that the deceased was aged about 65 years at the time of accident and appellant are the legal heirs of the deceased, the Tribunal considering the same has deducted 1/3 of the income towards his personal and living expenses, applied '7' as multiplier and awarded just compensation which does not call for interference in the appeal.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants- claimants, learned counsel for respondent No.4-insurer, having NC: 2023:KHC-D:13208-DB perused the memorandum of appeal and the Tribunal records, the only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is:
Whether the appellants-claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation?
6.
The answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reasons.
7. The parties to the proceeding do not dispute that Sri. Shreepati, has died in the road accident occurred on 13.08.2012 and the appellants are the legal heirs of the deceased.
The insurer does not dispute its liability.

The Tribunal while assessing income of the deceased has notionally assessed at Rs.5,000/- per month on the ground that the documents available on record are not sufficient to substantiate the claim of income of the deceased.

8. This Court has perused the oral and documentary evidence more particularly Exs.P.10 and P.11,
the bank statements produced by the appellants-claimants.

No doubt two entries in the bank statement reflect different amounts as pension amount, however, that itself is not sufficient to come to the conclusion that the deceased was earning Rs.9,867/- per NC: 2023:KHC-D:13208-DB month as claimed by the appellants.

Bare perusal of the aforesaid Exhibits clearly indicates different amounts in both Exhibits, there cannot be variation in pension and no pension papers were placed on record to ascertain the correct position.
Hence contention of the appellant has no merit and is rejected.

9. This Court, at Lok Adalath assesses notional income in the motor vehicle cases based on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the purpose of assessing income of the deceased in the absence of cogent and acceptable evidence on record.

In the instant case, the A. Prashanth Kumar vs Naga Raju S/O Basappa on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173363978/
4 evidence on record is not sufficient to come to the conclusion that the deceased was earning a particular amount as there are discrepancies in the amount shown in the bank statements at Exs.P.10 and P.11.

sentences.text: Hence, this Court assesses the income of the deceased at Rs.6,500/- per month basing its reliance on the aforesaid chart.
The Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd of the same towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and applied '7' multiplier and the same do not call for interference.

Thus the claimants are entitled for compensation towards loss of dependency at Rs.3,63,972/- (Rs.6,500/- x 12 x 7 x 1/3).

Keeping in mind the ratio of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1 the appellants-claimants are entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
